name: Encoded polyline algorithm format encode and decode
description: Encode a list of [latitude, longitude] pairs into the compact encoded-polyline text format (delta, zigzag, 5-bit chunks, precision 0-13; default 5), or decode such text back to coordinates.

provenance.metadata_source: public GitHub repository API (license field and created_at), observed this mining round; actual license file inspected
provenance.reference_values: Every case input comes from upstream test/polyline.test.js; eleven assert literal upstream expected strings or arrays. Full outputs, including the identity-test inputs, were generated by executing the pinned upstream src/polyline.js in Node, not this port; one supplementary decode is labelled. reference/verify_upstream.py reruns upstream locally.

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after 10 seconds. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

limitations: Coordinates are [latitude, longitude] numbers (an optional third value is ignored, as upstream); no datum, projection, GeoJSON flipping, range validation of latitude/longitude or route semantics. Values are rounded half away from zero at 10^precision. Scaled values must stay below 2^52 for exactness. Decoding is stricter than upstream: characters outside ASCII 63..126 and truncated values are rejected instead of silently producing coordinates.
port_notes: Port of py2_round, encode, polyline.encode and polyline.decode from src/polyline.js at the pinned commit: Python-2-style rounding, delta from previous rounded point, zigzag sign mapping, 5-bit little-endian chunks with 0x20 continuation and offset 63. JavaScript float shifting (coordinate /= 32, & 0x1f, multiply-by-shift accumulation) is replaced by equivalent exact integer arithmetic within the documented 2^52 bound. fromGeoJSON/toGeoJSON are not exposed.
